'''Deane Montgomery''' (September 2, 1909 – March 15, 1992) was an American mathematician specializing in [[topology]] who was one of the contributors to the final resolution of [[Hilbert's fifth problem]] in the 1950s.  He served as president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] from 1961 to 1962.

Born in the small town of [[Weaver, Minnesota]], he received his [[B.S.]] from [[Hamline University]] in [[St. Paul, MN]] and his [[Master's degree|Master's]] and [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Iowa]] in 1933; his dissertation advisor was Edward Chittenden.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Montgomery.html |title=Montgomery biography |publisher=History.mcs.st-and.ac.uk |access-date=2011-03-15}}</ref>

In 1941 Montgomery was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]. In 1988, he was awarded the [[American Mathematical Society]] [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement.

He was a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deane Montgomery |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/deane-montgomery-tem3df/ |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> the [[American Philosophical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Deane+Montgomery&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> and of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deane Montgomery |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/deane-montgomery |access-date=2022-12-13 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref>
